To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have found a high-molecular complex with acid phosphates activity in the cytoplasm of human mammary tumor, which is not present in normal mammary gland.
we have identified a new high molecular weight complex of acid phosphatase in human breast cancer.

1) a high-molecular-weight complex with acid phosphotase activity is present in the cytosolic fraction of human mammary carcinomas; 2) this enzyme has an apparent molecular weight of 106; 3) it is active on typical acid phosphatases substrates such as ATP and PPi; 4) it is not inhibited by L-(+) tartrate, and 5) it is also present in some samples of non-neoplastic mammary tissues
In summary, our research is concerned with
a large molecular weight complex with acid-phosphatase activity, present in human mammary tumors.
the presence of a high molecular weight complex with acid phophatase activity in cytosolic extracts from human mammary tumors.
the characterization of a high-molar mass complex with acid phosphatic activity present in human mammary tumors.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the enzyme is a complex with a molecular weight of 106 which is present in the cytosolic fraction and which is not disaggregated by SDS, but which yields several polypeptides in its reduced state.
the enzyme complex is a high-molecular-weight protein which is present in human mammary tissues and which is not a typical lysosomal enzyme.

this complex is a high-molecular-weight protein, with an apparent molecular weight of 106, that hydrolyzes p-NPP, ATP and PPi, that it is not inhibited by tartrate, that it is resistant to heat and SDS and that its presence is related to breast cancer.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this enzyme complex is not a simple enzyme, and it may be related to the tumor cell growth.
the high-molecular weight form of acid phosphatase found in human breast cancer is not a tumor-associated enzyme.
the presence of this high-molecular weight enzyme complex in breast cancer cytosols could be used as a marker for the presence of malignant cells in the mammary tissue.

the presence of this complex in human breast cancer may be a useful marker for the detection of this type of tumor.
